provenance_note: The IEC 61131-3 block semantics and the lumped-model solutions are re-derived at run time by a reference implementation that does not call the block runtime or the integration loop; those cases carry ref_source recomputed. Cases whose reference is an authored sequence carry ref_source recorded. Author-run benchmark against independent references, not an independent validation.
reference: Independent re-implementation of the IEC 61131-3 standard function blocks, closed-form solutions of the lumped balances the plant model declares, and closed-form evaluation of the discrete control algebra.
reference_citations: IEC 61131-3:2025, Edition 4.0 (2025-05), Programmable controllers - Part 3: Programming languages: Table 44 standard bistable function blocks (SR, RS), Table 45 standard edge detection function blocks (R_TRIG, F_TRIG), Table 47 and Figure 17 standard timer function blocks and their timing diagrams (TP, TON, TOF). https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/68533

Reference implementation refExec() inside this artifact harness: a second implementation of those tables, written for the benchmark, which counts whole scans instead of accumulating elapsed time and never calls the tool block runtime. 34 block configurations are driven for 400 scans each from a fixed LCG seed and compared scan by scan.

Closed-form solutions of the balances the plant model declares: h(t) = h0 + (Qin - Qout) t / A for a tank of constant area, and C dT/dt = q - UA (T - Tout) with solution T(t) = Tinf + (T0 - Tinf) exp(-UA t / C), Tinf = Tout + q / UA, for a lumped zone. Evaluated outside the integration loop.
tolerance: Exact for categorical results, for arithmetic whose operands and result are exactly representable in binary64, and for the identities the model states about itself (a frozen integrator, a stuck actuator). For time-marched cases the bound is N eps max(1, |ref|), where N is the number of solver substeps that case actually takes (scans times ceil(scan / plant step)) and eps = 2^-52; where the criterion is a threshold crossing the bound is one integration step of the solver itself. No absolute bound is placed on a dimensional quantity.
not_benchmarked: Conformance to IEC 61131-3 is not certified: the standard function blocks named in the citations are compared against an independent implementation of the same tables, and nothing else in the standard is covered.
No vendor runtime is emulated and no vendor-specific block, addressing or task model is tested.

Air transport between zones is absent from the plant model, so fan and damper states do not enter the energy balance. Two cases record that boundary; the physics behind it is not modelled and therefore not benchmarked.
Real controller timing - scan jitter, I/O latency, task pre-emption - is outside the model: simulation time advances in exact multiples of the declared scan period.
The interface, the trend chart and the printed report are not covered by this artifact.
No case tests numerical behaviour of a user-built project larger than the shipped examples.

Constant-area mass balance: h(t) = h0 - Q t / A.
The level is held at the declared maximum once the tank is full.
With the tank full the spilled rate equals the net inflow.
C dT/dt = -UA (T - Tout) with solution Tout + (T0 - Tout) exp(-UA t / C).
A zone under a constant heat input settles at Tout + q/UA. An uncontrolled zone that receives coil power therefore has a steady state fixed by UA alone.
With UA = 0 the zone integrates its gain: T = T0 + q t / C.
Rate-limited travel: position = rate * t while the command is ahead of it.

Sensors are sampled into the input image before the plant advances (IEC 61131-3 scan model), so the reading after n scans is the first-order lag at (n-1) scan periods, not at n. Over 1.0 s at scan 0.1 s this is exp(-0.9), not exp(-1.0).
Running feedback appears on the first scan after the declared start delay has elapsed, and the input image is one scan behind the plant.
An accumulator closed through DELAY advances by one per scan: after three scans it reads 3.
A feedback path with no scan boundary in it is refused rather than solved.

Air transport is absent from the model: the zone energy balance takes heat only from the coils, so a failed fan moves the room temperature by exactly zero. Declared in the tool limitations.

The loops of this preset act on supply-air temperature, and a PI with a finite Ti leaves no steady-state offset.

No block in this preset reads AI_ROOM, so the room carries no loop. Combined with zone-equilibrium that fixes its steady state at Tout + q/UA, which at the settled coil command is 306.15 K against a 295.15 K setpoint.
